title: FDIC-Insured Bank Branch Locations
publisher: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) BankFind Suite
notes: All FDIC-insured bank offices in Philadelphia, Montgomery and Delaware counties within 1.5 mi of a site; kept full-service brick-and-mortar/retail offices and limited-service drive-thru/retail facilities, dropped trust, administrative, messenger, mobile/seasonal and loan-production offices. Website is the institution's FDIC-listed web address.

title: Credit Union Offices (NCUA Credit Union Locator)
notes: Federally insured credit union sites returned by NCUA's locator within 2 mi of each site address, kept within 1.5 mi; ATM-only sites dropped. Many are workplace or church-based credit unions with restricted membership; the field of membership is in the detail line. Credit union type and website from NCUA's credit union profile.

title: PA CareerLink Philadelphia Centers and Outreach Sites
license: Published on pacareerlinkphl.org; no open license stated
notes: Marker list behind the 'Career Centers' map on PA CareerLink Philadelphia's contact page: the four full-time comprehensive centers, the Northeast Hub, part-time outreach sites (mostly in Free Library branches) and partner sites. Used instead of data.pa.gov's CareerLink Locations (6p38-7dgx, last updated 2022), which still lists the old West Philadelphia address.

title: Workforce and Employment Resources (Office of Black Male Engagement Directory)
publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Black Male Engagement
license: City of Philadelphia open data (OpenDataPhilly terms of use)
notes: Organizations in the City's public resource directory (public_yn = Y) whose listed services include workforce development or employment; most are multi-service nonprofits rather than job centers. Emails dropped.

title: Vacant Land and Land Bank Parcels (within 1 mile)
publisher: City of Philadelphia (Dept. of Planning & Development / L&I Vacant Property Indicators; Office of Property Assessment)
license: City of Philadelphia open data (OpenDataPhilly terms of use)
notes: Parcels the City's Vacant Property Indicators model flags as likely vacant land (4902), plus Philadelphia Land Bank-owned parcels from OPA (9 not flagged vacant, 301 in both), within 1 mile of a site; polygons reduced to an interior point. owner_type is derived from the OPA owner name (public = City, Land Bank, PRA, PHA, PHDC, School District, state, federal, SEPTA etc.; 1347 public); private owner names are not kept. 'Likely vacant' is a model result, not a field survey.

sources.title: OPA Properties (owner = Philadelphia Land Bank)
sources.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Property Assessment

title: Public Housing and LIHTC Properties
publisher: U.S. Dept. of Housing and Urban Development (HUD eGIS); City of Philadelphia (PHA Senior Sites layer)
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work); PHA Senior Sites: City of Philadelphia open data (OpenDataPhilly terms of use)
data_date: PHA developments 2026-10-06; LIHTC: latest placed-in-service year among these records 2017 (HUD layer updated 2025-05-14)
notes: Philadelphia Housing Authority developments from HUD (27; one point per development at its largest building), City-hosted PHA senior sites (6; merged into the matching development where one is nearby) and HUD LIHTC properties (190) within 1.5 mi; same-name records within 40 m are merged (2 PHA developments also carry LIHTC, units not summed across programs). HUD's public housing layer omits PHA properties converted to Section 8 under RAD. 12 LIHTC properties targeted to homeless households or named as recovery/DV/emergency housing were left out per the sensitive-location rule. Old LIHTC projects (1987-2000s) may be past their affordability period. Feature counts by source: {'hud_public_housing_developments': 27, 'pha_senior_sites': 6, 'hud_lihtc': 188}.

title: City-Funded Affordable Housing Production
publisher: City of Philadelphia, Dept. of Planning & Development, Division of Housing and Community Development
license: City of Philadelphia open data (OpenDataPhilly terms of use)
notes: DHCD-funded rental, homeownership and mixed-use projects (complete and under construction) within 1.5 mi; year is the fiscal year completed (blank when under construction). 62 'Special Needs' (supportive, recovery, shelter-type) projects were left out per the sensitive-location rule.
